newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia crude, condensate forecast cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia crude, condensate forecast cut.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecaster on Tuesday sharply cut its forecast for Australian crude oil and condensate production for 1996/97 (June/July), seeing 1.5 percent growth to 30.7 billion litres.

The forecast, in the March quarter bulletin of the Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Resource Economics (ABARE), compares with the December quarter forecast of seven percent growth to 32.3 billion litres.
ABARE said technical problems and bad weather had slowed production at some of the newer projects on the North West Shelf off Western Australia.
However, production for 1997/98 is forecast to rise 6.2 percent to 32.6 billion litres as new projects reached peak output.

ABARE also revised up its trade weighted crude oil price forecast to US$19 a barrel in 1997, down five percent on 1996 due to increased supply. The price was expected to continue to decline to US$18.55 in 1998, the forecaster said.
Crude oil production in the Gippsland Basin was forecast to rise in 1996/97 by up to five percent after three years in which production fell by 10 percent a year.

ABARE said recent announcements on oil and gas developments would have a significant impact on production in the medium to longer term, although the projects were not expected to come on stream before 1999.

"The granting of production licences for two oil projects in the Timor Sea - Elang/Kakatua inside the Zone of Co-Operation and Laminaria/Corallina just outside the Zone - could eventually boost output in the region by as much as 170,000 barrels a day," ABARE said.
Crude oil and condensate exports were forecast to rise 13 percent in 1996/97 and a further 10 percent in 1997/98.
Total earnings from crude oil, condensate and LPG exports were forecast to rise more than A$500 million to A$2.4 billion in 1996/97 and by a further A$70 million in 1997/98.
